div.l: But soth to seyn I ne wote how men hym call
A clerk þere was of Oxenford / also
That vn to logyk hade long ygo
And lene was his hors as yt were a rake
And he was nat right fat I vndretake
But loked holow and þere to soberly
Full thredebare was his oủerest courtby
For he hade yit gete hym no benefice
Ne was nat worldly to haue an office
For hym were leủer to haue at his beddes hede
xxᵗⁱ bokes clad in blak and rede
Of Aristotle and his philosophie
Than riche robes or fethell or sautrye
But all be it þogh he were a philosophre
Yit hade he but litell gold in his cofre
But all þat he from his frendes hent
On bokes and on lernyng he it spent
And besy gan for the soules pray
Of hem þat yaf hym wherwᵗith to scoley
And stody toke he most cure and hede
Noght a worde spake he more þan nede
And þat was seide in fourme and reủerence
And short and quyk and full of hiegh sentence
Sownyng in morall v̉ertue was his speche
And gladly wold he lerne and gladly wold he tche
A sergeant of lawe þere was ware and wys
That full oft hade be at pavys
That was ryche of excellence
Discrete he was and of grete reủerence
He semed swych his wordes were so wys
Iustice hade he be full oft in assise
Both by patent and plein cōmmissiou
For his science and his hiegh renou
Of fees and robes hade he many on
So grete a purchasour was nowhere non
Al was fee simple to him in effect
His p̉erchasyng might nat ben in suspect
Nowhere so besy a man as he þere nas
And yitt / he semed besyer þan he was
In t̉ermes hade he cas and domes all
